text: Okay, this is a scheduling problem on a directed graph. Sessions are nodes and each prerequisite pair is an edge, and I need a valid order, which is a topological sort. If there's a cycle there's no valid order. Can I assume there may be several valid orders and any is fine, and what should I return if there's a cycle?
Good — and yes, any valid order is fine; if there's a cycle, return an empty array. Let me put it up on your screen.

text: I'll use Kahn's algorithm. Build the adjacency list and in-degrees, start a queue with all zero in-degree sessions, pop one at a time, add it to the order and decrement its neighbours, pushing any that reach zero. If the order has fewer than n sessions at the end there was a cycle, so I return an empty array. Time is O of V plus E and space is O of V plus E.
